title.text: Atlas Hub — combined direction (1 + 2), in three colourways

shared.text: The A+B combination: Notion's calm structure — teamspace sidebar, a Business section that appears when a business exists, a real database table for shared tasks — but the Home is a LIVING page (your Brief, Today, Business at a glance), never blank. Same layout in all three colours so you can pick by eye. Colour-blind accessibility is built into every one: status shows an icon and a word, never colour alone.

capA.text: Warm Paper — light, the closest to Notion's own calm. Cream sidebar, warm-orange accent, generous space.

capB.text: Ember Dark — the command-center feel: deep slate, warm ember accent, the same layout at rest in the dark.

capC.text: Access — a blue/amber palette that stays distinct for every kind of colour vision (red–green and blue–yellow), higher contrast throughout. This is also what 'colour-blind mode' switches any theme to.

capPhone.text: Phone — same home, one thumb. Bottom tab bar reaches Home, Calendar, Messages, Business and Settings. Built to run on new and older handsets: large touch targets, safe-area padding for notches, and no bleeding-edge CSS.

capCust.text: Customise & access — theme, a pick-your-own accent, text size, density, colour-blind mode, and 'When Atlas may pop up' (only-when-I-ask / urgent / anything). Home cards rearrange or hide. Stored on your machine.

capSound.text: Sound & voice — Atlas's voice (with audition), speaking volume, when it speaks aloud, the wake word (heard on-device, nothing leaves), the mic with a live level, quiet hours, and a one-tap Mute. A quick volume + mute also sits in the top bar and every pop-up.

capGestures.text: Gestures — an accessibility setting that shows its own state and teaches itself. The top says plainly whether it's On and that the camera's in use (read on-device, nothing leaves). Below is the real vocabulary Atlas ships — thumb up/down to answer, pinch to pick up, ring to confirm, hooked strokes to scroll, fist to undo, palm out to stop — each shown with what it does, grouped and colour-blind-safe (icon + words). Holding up one finger brings this list back on screen any time. Two honest rails: a gesture can decline but never approves anything irreversible (that still needs your voice or a tap), and gestures are optional — everything is also sayable or clickable. You can teach your own, which win over the defaults.

sectInner.text: Two inner pages — how work and thinking get shown

capNow.text: Now — Atlas's thought process, live. Not a raw log: a legible stream of the plan, what it's doing, when it hands a step to a worker, when it VERIFIES, and when it hits a wall and reroutes rather than cutting a corner. The rail shows its time budget and the fallback route. 'Plain / Detailed' controls how much reasoning you see.

capOut.text: Outstanding — the open backlog, personal and business together. Waiting-on-you, then Blocked (each with the honest triple: what it TRIED, what STOPPED it, what it NEEDS from you), In progress (with who's building it), and Carried-over (with how many days). Nothing rots quietly.

sectPop.text: Pop-ups — the same two, without opening the hub

capPanels.text: Desktop pop-ups — Atlas floats these over your screen, no hub needed. An ambient 'here's what I'm doing' panel and a 'ready for you' pop-up. Top-right shows the collapsed pill; both dismiss with ×. Only appear when it's urgent or when you ask.

capAlerts.text: Phone pop-ups — a live-activity card + Dynamic-Island pill for the thought process, and an actionable notification for what needs you (Implement / Read / Later on the alert). Ongoing notification on Android, Live Activity on iOS.

sectGive.text: Give Atlas something — link, photo, video, or any file

capGiveDesk.text: Desktop — one ask bar with a '+' to attach: paste a link, a photo or video, or ANY file — zip, PDF, spreadsheet, any type, any size — or pull it from your phone. Drag-and-drop works the same. A 2.4 GB backup unpacks and reads in the background, so a big file never blocks you. 'Handed to Atlas lately' keeps what you've fed it in reach.

capGivePhone.text: Phone — no separate app to open. From anything (a browser, Photos, Files), tap Share and Atlas is the first target. It reads the item on your phone and hands it to your Atlas at home — nothing goes anywhere else. 'Sent to Atlas' confirms, then you can add it to a project or save it as a concept.

sectTrust.text: First run & sharing out — the safety-precaution clauses, in plain words

capSetup.text: First run — three short steps. Step 2 says the important part plainly: Atlas runs on this machine, your data stays with you, and it's provided as-is at your own risk. One checkbox to acknowledge — the clause as a calm safety precaution, not a wall of legalese.

capShareOut.text: Sharing out — before anything leaves your machine, Atlas asks. It names exactly what goes (this one file) and who gets it (Jordan's Atlas, encrypted), and states plainly they see nothing else on your machine. Answer by voice ('yes' / 'no', gated to your own voice) or by button. This is the consent step, reused from calls, applied to documents.

sectFlow.text: Talk to Atlas, and let it work the in-betweens

capTalk.text: Talk to Atlas — from the hub, and front-and-centre on phone. Hold to talk, or type instead. You give it a whole errand in one breath ('send the Q3 report to Jordan, then remind me to call him at four') and it does the middle: the send goes through with no prompt because Jordan is trusted, and the reminder is set. Atlas speaks its reply and still shows an Undo.

capTrusted.text: Trusted recipients — pre-approve the people you share with often, so routine things flow instead of stopping you. Per person, and per kind: Jordan auto-gets business docs and tasks but personal always asks; a friend not trusted yet still prompts for everything. A master 'always ask' override, and an undo window you set. The point isn't fewer safeguards — it's not asking twice for the same trusted, routine move.

capShareAuto.text: The trusted path — no modal. A corner heads-up ('Sent to Jordan'), a countdown Undo, and a plain line that personal files still ask first. This is what 'Atlas works the in-betweens' looks like: the confirm is spent only where it earns its place.

sectMsg.text: Messages — same hub, same trust rules, its own room

capMsg.text: Messages — WhatsApp/GroupMe-shaped, but inside the hub and end-to-end encrypted, Atlas-to-Atlas with no server in between. One-to-ones and groups (Northwind project). The key consistency: sharing a document IN a chat obeys the SAME trusted rule as everywhere else — a business doc to Jordan (trusted) sends with a heads-up and an Undo, a personal file or a non-trusted person still asks first. Sending is instant and stamped at your local time; if they're offline, Atlas holds it and delivers when they're back, keeping the send timestamp.

capMsgPhone.text: Messages on phone — iPhone and Android, the delivery model shown honestly: a message to Sam (offline) reads 'Sent · held for Sam', with a plain line that it delivers the moment Sam's back, still stamped at the time you sent it. No waiting on the other person to be online before you can send.

sectPages.text: The inner pages — Calendar, Projects, Clients, Documents, Business

capCal.text: Calendar — built into Atlas, on your machine, and it mirrors your iPhone/Android calendar both ways. No TimeTree, no account. Personal / business / system are separate calendars you toggle — each event carries a word-label (Personal, Northwind, System), not colour alone, so it reads for every kind of colour vision. The right rail is today; the top bar shows the two-way sync and offline state plainly.

capProj.text: Projects — a Notion-style workshop page, not a ticket. The doc holds the goal, a task checklist (with who owns each — Atlas or you), and the honest result: proven in a copy, guards green, nothing merged until you approve. The right rail is Atlas's build stream for THIS project — planned, wrote, hit a wall and rerouted, verified, waiting on you — plus the files it touched in the copy. Same stream as Now, scoped to one thing.

capClient.text: Client record — a business contact (Maya · Riverstone) with the firewall made visible. Alongside the usual contact fields and activity, a 'What Maya can see' panel spells out exactly what's crossed to her (two shared items, encrypted) and — with plain no-marks — what hasn't: nothing personal, no other clients. The firewall isn't a setting buried in options; it's shown on the record itself.

capDocs.text: Documents — everything on your machine, one list. Area tags (Personal / Northwind / Homelab) keep the firewall legible, and a 'Shared' column shows for each file whether it's Private or gone out and to whom (Maya, Jordan) — the same trusted rules, made auditable. Any size lives here too: the 2.4 GB backup sits in the list like anything else.

capOverview.text: Business overview — Northwind at a glance, cleanly separate from personal. Open tasks (with who owns each), active clients, invoiced vs paid, and what's awaiting payment, then shared tasks and the partner/client roster, closed by Atlas's plain-language read: one invoice overdue, nudge drafted and waiting on your yes; a renewal in three weeks. The business face of the same hub.

sectStates.text: The details you asked for — one calendar, dark mode everywhere, and the states in between

capCalWeek.text: All events, one calendar. The week view puts personal, business and system on a single time grid — nothing separate to stitch together — with a real time axis so a time-blocked stretch (the hatched 'Deep work' blocks) reads as booked time, not just a dot. 'All calendars' is the default; you can still hide one. Day / Week / Month across the top.

capCalDark.text: The exact same calendar in Ember Dark — proof that light/dark isn't just the home screen. The theme is one set of tokens the whole hub reads, so every page built here (Calendar, Messages, Projects, Clients, Documents, Overview, Settings) turns dark together, desktop and phone. Set it in Settings or Appearance; 'Match system' follows the OS.

capEmpty.text: First-run home — the answer to 'don't make it blank'. Before there's any data, home is a warm welcome with three or four guided steps (connect a calendar, add a mailbox, hand Atlas a file, optionally add a business) — skippable, and it works offline the whole time. The business section only appears once you add one.

capOffline.text: Offline — the offline-first promise, shown honestly. A calm amber banner ('you're offline, and Atlas is still working'), then two columns: what's live (calendar, files, drafting, the build, voice) and what's waiting (mailbox sync, queued messages and shares). The queued items send themselves in order, with original timestamps, when you reconnect.

capSettings.text: Settings index — one place that ties it together. Appearance is up top with the light / dark / Access / match-system picker, labelled 'applies to the whole hub', then cards for Sound & voice, Trusted recipients, Notifications & pop-ups, Calendars & accounts, and Data & privacy. Everything stored on your machine.
